sentences.text: Revenue went from nothing in FY2021 to $5.39 billion in FY2025, a 48.1% three-year CAGR from FY2022 [F7][D342].
The step change came in FY2022, when revenue rose 2914.5% to $1.66 billion on increased deliveries of 19,412 vehicles [F4][D83][P67].
FY2023 added 167.4% to $4.43 billion on 29,790 more deliveries, higher average selling prices and non-Rivian trade-ins [F5][D135][P56].
Growth then stalled: revenue rose 12.1% in FY2024 and 8.4% in FY2025, while the operating loss narrowed 23.5% to $3.59 billion [F6][F7][F26][D187][D239][D240].
In FY2025 Software and Services contributed 21.6pp of growth and reached 28.9% of revenue, while New electric vehicles fell 12.5% and subtracted 10.5pp [D295][D293][D287][D288].

Software and services revenue rose 221.7% primarily on vehicle electrical architecture and software development services from the Joint Venture, plus remarketing and repair and maintenance [S14][D294][P18].
Automotive revenue fell 14.6% as deliveries dropped 9,332 vehicles, partly from the expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025 [S23][D315][P22].
Operating costs grew 6.9% against revenue growth of 8.4%, so operating costs grew 1.5pp slower than revenue [D258][D239][D266].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% in FY2025 while the net loss fell 23.2%, so EPS improved 34.5% to -$3.07 [D260][D241][F57][D243].
Gross margin turned positive at 2.7% in FY2025, above the -45.8% window median and the -845.5% window low [F19][D332][D330].
Operating margin of -66.5% is the window high but still far below the -1.6% autos peer median, at the 25th percentile of four peers [F31][D325][D344][D343].

The FY2025 operating margin improved 27.8pp, almost entirely from cost of revenue (+26.8pp), as Automotive cost of revenues fell on fewer vehicles produced and lower material and conversion costs [D253][D267][P21].
In FY2025 net margin of -67.7% sat 1.1pp below the -66.5% operating margin, with other expense of $54 million partly from a $186 million securities litigation settlement [F43][F31][D359][X84][P10].
Operating cash flow improved to -$779 million in FY2025 from -$1.72 billion, primarily driven by a significant reduction in net loss [F64][F63][P4].
Free cash flow was -$2.49 billion, a -46.2% margin, the window high but below the 6.6% autos peer median [F78][D226][D334][D348].
Capex of $1.71 billion was 31.7% of revenue and 2.18x D&A, up from 23.0% of revenue in FY2024 [F71][D225][D228][D173].
Capex rose 49.9% on expansion of production capacity at the Normal Factory and next-generation platforms [D246][P3].
Net cash fell to $1.64 billion, or 30.5% of revenue, from $3.26 billion a year earlier, as cash and investments dropped 21.0% to $6.08 billion [D231][D232][D179][D229][D261].
The current ratio fell to 2.33x, the window low, from 4.70x, as current liabilities grew 64.1% [F129][D339][F128][D251].
Financing cash flow of $886 million came mainly from $750 million of Class A shares issued to Volkswagen Group on the Financial Milestone [F92][P2].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% in FY2025, and stock-based compensation was 20.7% of the operating loss [D260][D237].
Net losses have persisted for seven straight years, from -$426 million in FY2019 to -$3.65 billion in FY2025 [R1][F32][F38].
The loss is narrowing, but seven years without a profit leaves the model dependent on external financing [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last five years [R2][D223][D31][D67][D119][D171].
That dilution burden is large relative to a business still far from breakeven [R2].
Cash and investments cover 2.4 years of the latest burn [R3][D236].
Runway is adequate but shrinking as net cash falls each year [R3].
Whether gross margin holds above the FY2025 2.7% level, in the FY2026 10-K [F19].
Whether operating cash flow improves past the FY2025 -$779 million toward breakeven, in the FY2026 10-K [F64].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays above the FY2025 30.5% level, in the FY2026 10-K [D232].
